correctness.rationale: Multiplication by z1 is an isometric identification with the radial Bergman subspace divisible by z1; monomial orthogonality subtracts the kernel independent of z1 and divides difference by t=z1̄w1. This gives C[(1-u-t)^(-s)-(1-u)^(-s)]/t, s=d+α+1, with nonzero t=0 continuation. Cauchy–Schwarz gives |u|+|t|<1 and |q|<1, while axis points attain every |q|<1. Principal logarithm of 1-q lies in right-half-plane strip, zeros require q=1-e^(2πij/s), j≠0. Strict |q|=2sin(π|j|/s)<1 iff 0<6|j|<s; derivative of numerator nonzero gives scalar simplicity and staircase 2(ceil(s/6)-1). Cases s=6,7,12,13 separately checked. Full proof infinite in d and α, not numerical extrapolation.
